chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali عليه السلام used to say:

There is no harm in a boy giving the adhan before he reaches puberty, but he should not lead in prayer until he reaches puberty. If he does lead, his prayer is valid, but the prayer of those behind him is invalid.

key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: a boy who has not yet reached full maturity
key_terms.فَسَدَتْ صَلَاةُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ: the salat (prayer) of those praying behind him became invalid
key_terms.يَؤُمَّ: to lead others as Imam in salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنَ: to give the adhan, the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a boy who has not yet reached puberty give the adhan or lead salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith sets a legal distinction between a prepubescent boy giving the adhan and leading salat (prayer). It permits his adhan before puberty, but does not allow him to serve as Imam for others; if he does, his own salat (prayer) is valid while the salat (prayer) of the followers is invalid.
